the geographic proximity of organizations and the institutional commitments of network members are both important determinants of the spillover of knowledge across contractual ties.
the effects of spillovers in the biotech industry are moderated by geographic propinquity (proximity to other firms) and organizational form (alliances vs. other ties).
the effects of network position are conditional on the institutional context of the network and that the effects of institutional context are conditional on network position.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
knowledge networks are conduits of spillovers that are a function of geographic proximity and the openness of network nodes to information sharing.
the network of biotech firms in Boston is a knowledge network.
the network structure of a region is not a sufficient condition to explain the diffusion of knowledge and technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Boston biotech community is a relatively open network in terms of the flow of information and knowledge among its members, and that this openness is associated with the presence of large, publicly traded firms that are committed to open disclosure of their research.
the Boston biotechnology network is a highly integrated system of information exchange and knowledge transfer that is organized around a set of highly connected core firms.
the effects of networks as conduits for knowledge spillovers depend on the institutional environment and the organizational forms that characterize the network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flow of information is a function of the structure of interorganizational networks, but that the nature of the network itself depends on the institutional context in which it is embedded.
knowledge spillovers are a function of both the network structure and the institutional commitments of its members.
the flow of information within an innovation network is not a function solely of the structure of the network, but rather of the context in which the network is embedded.
